You are the implementing engineer for Atlas ERP, in '/Users/taha/Claude projects/expremental ERP/atlas-erp' on branch feat/perf-smoke (dev merged; Phase 4 finance complete). NO git commands. uv at ~/.local/bin/uv; run `cd backend && ~/.local/bin/uv run <cmd>`. PostgreSQL 16 at postgresql+asyncpg://atlas:atlas@localhost:55432/atlas.

READ FIRST (binding): PERFORMANCE.md §5 (perf suite: @pytest.mark.perf, separate NON-BLOCKING CI job on SQLite, locally against Postgres before promotions; budgets: list p95 <300ms, statements/aging <1.5s, dashboard <500ms — SQLite CI numbers at 2× as a looser smoke) + §2 (bulk inserts for the dataset itself); CLAUDE.md; STRUCTURE.md; .github/workflows/ci.yml (current jobs; you ADD a new non-blocking perf job — it must NOT become a required status check, so name it distinctly e.g. 'perf-smoke'). Then read existing: backend/pyproject.toml (markers), backend/tests/conftest.py (template-copy harness, query counter), backend/tests/modules/finance/factories.py (builders), backend/app/modules/finance/service/statements/* (what TB/P&L read), service/ar_aging.py, service/journal_read.py (list), bank/bank_import.py bulk-insert pattern as reference. Latest migration = 0019.

TASK — PLAN 4P.7: tests/perf/ smoke suite. Build:

1. `backend/tests/perf/conftest.py`:
   - register nothing globally; a SESSION-scoped `perf_dataset` fixture that builds ONE mid-volume tenant on a dedicated SQLite file DB (own template copy or fresh migrate — reuse the template-copy machinery if clean): seed via BULK inserts (Core executemany — per PERFORMANCE §2; the seeding itself must finish in well under a minute): a COA (~30 accounts incl. AR control/revenue/tax/bank), one fiscal year with 12 open periods, **~20,000 posted journal lines** across ~2,500 entries spread over the year (vary accounts, dates, cost centers; set is_posted/posting_date/fiscal_period_id denormalization correctly + entry headers POSTED — write them directly via bulk inserts under system_context/tenant_context, NOT through post_entry (that would take minutes); keep debits==credits per entry so statements balance), **~1,500 customer invoices** (mixed statuses/due dates, open_amounts) for aging, and a user with read permissions for API timing.
   - IMPORTANT: writing posted journal rows directly bypasses triggers? No — inserts of already-POSTED rows would hit the period trigger (INSERT trigger fires when status POSTED: period must be OPEN — keep all periods OPEN so inserts pass; the balance trigger only fires on UPDATE to POSTED, not raw INSERT of POSTED — verify against migration 0009's trigger events and ensure your insert path satisfies whichever fire; if the INSERT period trigger validates, keep periods open and dates in-range).
   - a `timed` helper: run a callable N times (e.g. 5 after 1 warmup), record wall-clock, return median (median is stabler than p95 with 5 samples; document that CI smoke uses median ≤ 2× budget).
2. `backend/tests/perf/test_budgets.py` (every test `@pytest.mark.perf`):
   - journal-entries list API (filtered by date range + paginated 50): median ≤ 600ms (2×300);
   - trial balance service call (full year): ≤ 3s (2×1.5);
   - P&L service call (full year): ≤ 3s;
   - AR aging service call: ≤ 3s;
   - balance sheet as-of year-end: ≤ 3s;
   - dataset sanity preconditions (row counts ≥ targets, TB balanced) so a silently-small dataset can't fake a pass.
   Tests run the SERVICE functions directly where API auth would dominate (statements), and the API path for the list (closer to user-perceived). Print the measured times (always, via a report line) so CI logs show trends.
3. `backend/pyproject.toml`: add the `perf` marker; ensure default runs EXCLUDE perf (`-m "not pg"` currently — tests must also be excluded from the plain CI run: update the CI backend job's SQLite step to `-m "not pg and not perf"`, and the pg step stays `-m pg`).
4. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: new job `perf-smoke` (NOT in branch-protection contexts — do not rename existing jobs): runs on ubuntu, setup-uv, `uv run pytest -q -m perf` with `continue-on-error: true` so it never blocks merges (PERFORMANCE §5 'non-blocking'), and prints the timing report. 
5. `Makefile`: `perf` target (`cd backend && uv run pytest -q -m perf -s`).
6. docs: PERFORMANCE-related note in docs/modules/finance.md or a short tests/perf/README? NO README files in modules — add a paragraph to docs/architecture.md? Simplest sanctioned home: extend the PERF section note in docs/modules/core.md (testing strategy already lives there) with 3 lines on the perf suite. 
7. Update PLAN.md (tick 4P.7) + PROGRESS.md. Run the suite locally against Postgres too (set ATLAS_DATABASE_URL...? the perf fixtures build their own SQLite file — for the Postgres variant, allow `ATLAS_PERF_DATABASE_URL` env override so `make perf` against pg works; run it once against the local pg and report timings; budgets asserted at 1× (300ms/1.5s) when the URL is Postgres — per §5 budgets are defined against Postgres).

RULES: no TODO/stub; absolute imports; ruff + pytest green: default suite (`-m "not pg and not perf"`) 537+1 unchanged, perf suite passes locally on SQLite AND against the local Postgres; don't print file contents; files <400 lines. The dataset seeding MUST be fast (target <30s SQLite) — bulk executemany only.

Return: files created/changed, the measured timings (SQLite and Postgres) per budget test, dataset build time, CI job config summary, and deviations with one-line justification.

Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

1	# PERFORMANCE.md — Performance & Deployment-Cost Protocol (Mid-Build Addendum)
2	
3	You are receiving this addendum while the build is in progress. Integration procedure, do this FIRST:
4	1. Commit this file at the repo root. Add to CLAUDE.md: "All code MUST comply with PERFORMANCE.md. Re-read it after any compaction."
5	2. Add every requirement below as numbered tasks in PLAN.md. For code that already exists (core, journal engine, FX), add explicit **retrofit tasks** ("audit fin_journal_* indexes against PERFORMANCE §1", "add pagination + query-count test to existing journal list endpoint"). File a `tech-debt` issue per GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md §6 for each retrofit found non-compliant.
6	3. From now on, the Definition of Done for any endpoint includes the checklist in §6.
7	
8	Target: the entire system must run well for a 50-concurrent-user SME tenant on a single 4 vCPU / 8 GB VPS, with p95 latency under the budgets in §5 against the high-volume seed tenant.
9	
10	# 1. Database & Indexing
11	- Every foreign key column gets an index. No exceptions. Alembic migrations that add an FK without its index fail review.
12	- Every column used in a WHERE filter, ORDER BY, or JOIN in any list/report endpoint gets an index; composite indexes for the dominant filter combination (e.g., `(tenant_id, posting_date)` on journal lines, `(tenant_id, item_id, warehouse_id)` on stock moves). `tenant_id` leads every composite index since every query filters on it.
13	- Aggregations for dashboards/reports never scan unbounded history at request time: date-bounded queries with covering indexes, or (for the cash/AR/AP KPI cards) small per-tenant summary tables maintained by event handlers — pick per case and record the choice in DECISIONS.md.
14	- All money math in `Decimal`/NUMERIC end to end. No floats anywhere in financial paths (this is correctness, but float-to-decimal retrofits are also expensive — enforce now).
15	- Use `EXPLAIN` during development on the three heaviest queries per module against the high-volume tenant; paste the plan summary into the PR description's Design notes.
16	
17	# 2. Query Patterns (the N+1 ban)
18	- List endpoints execute O(1) queries, never O(n): explicit `selectinload`/`joinedload` for every relationship the response schema touches. Lazy-loading inside a response serialization loop is a `severity:major` bug.
19	- Enforce mechanically: a pytest fixture that counts SQL statements per request (SQLAlchemy event listener); every list-endpoint test asserts `query_count <= 3`. Add this fixture to tests/conftest.py as a retrofit task and apply it to existing endpoints.
20	- Bulk operations (MRP runs, payment runs, depreciation runs, seed loading) use bulk inserts/updates and set-based SQL, never per-row ORM loops over large sets.
21	- No SELECT *: load only the columns the schema needs on hot list endpoints (use `load_only` where models are wide).
22	
23	# 3. API Behavior
24	- Pagination is mandatory on every collection endpoint — cursor-based, default page size 50, hard max 200. An unpaginated list endpoint may not merge.
25	- Report endpoints accept and require date-range bounds; the report builder caps result rows (10k) and offers CSV export for anything larger, generated by streaming, not by materializing in memory.
26	- Responses gzip-compressed (middleware); ETag/If-None-Match on slow-changing reference data (COA, item master, settings).
27	- Long-running operations (MRP, payment runs, statement imports over 1k lines) execute as background jobs returning a job id + polling endpoint, never inside a request that can hit a proxy timeout.
28	
29	# 4. Frontend Discipline
30	- One screen = ideally one, max three API calls on initial render. Compose data server-side in purpose-built read endpoints rather than letting the UI stitch six requests.
31	- Data grid is virtualized (windowed rendering) — it must handle a 200-row page without DOM bloat.
32	- TanStack Query defaults: 30s staleTime on reference data, request deduplication on, no refetch storms on window focus for heavy reports.
33	- Route-level code splitting per module so the initial bundle stays small; production build target < 300 kB gzipped for the entry chunk.
34	
35	# 5. High-Volume Seed Tenant + Latency Budget Tests
36	- Extend seed.py with a `--volume` tenant: ≥100k journal lines, ≥50k stock moves, ≥10k orders, ≥5k items, 3 fiscal years — generated with bulk inserts (seeding itself must finish in minutes, which also proves §2 bulk patterns).
37	- Add `tests/perf/` (marked `@pytest.mark.perf`, run in CI as a separate non-blocking job against SQLite, and locally against Postgres before each promotion): journal list w/ filters, trial balance, P&L, AR aging, stock-on-hand, order list — each asserts a wall-clock budget. Budgets against the volume tenant on Postgres: list endpoints p95 < 300 ms, statements/aging < 1.5 s, dashboard < 500 ms. Tune the SQLite CI numbers to be a looser smoke (2× budget) so CI stays stable while still catching regressions.
38	- A perf test failure before promotion is treated as `severity:major`: file the issue, fix or consciously re-budget with rationale in DECISIONS.md — never delete the test.
39	
40	# 6. Per-Endpoint Definition of Done (extends the existing DoD)
41	[ ] FK + filter columns indexed  [ ] query-count assertion passes  [ ] paginated  [ ] money is Decimal  [ ] heavy work bulk/background  [ ] included in perf suite if it's a hot path
42	
43	# 7. Deployment Doc (add docs/deployment.md before v1 promotion)
44	- Reference single-VPS topology: nginx/Caddy serving the static frontend build + reverse-proxying FastAPI (uvicorn, 2× vCPU workers) + Postgres on the same box; docker-compose.prod.yml with resource limits and Postgres tuned (shared_buffers 2 GB, work_mem sane, autovacuum on).
45	- Sizing table: demo/eval = 1 vCPU/2 GB; SME ≤50 users = 4 vCPU/8 GB; ≤200 users = 8 vCPU/16 GB or split DB onto its own box. State plainly that the app tier is stateless (JWT) so horizontal scaling is "add a container behind the proxy."
46	- Backup section: nightly `pg_dump` + WAL archiving note; restore drill instructions.
47	- A short "why it stays fast" section pointing at §1–§3 so operators understand the guarantees.
48

1	# STRUCTURE.md — Folder Structure, Naming & File-Handling Protocol for Atlas ERP
2	
3	Place this file at the repo root alongside CLAUDE.md and GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md, and add to CLAUDE.md: "All file creation, naming, and placement MUST follow STRUCTURE.md. Re-read it after any compaction." The rule of this document: **every file has exactly one correct home, and its name alone tells you what's inside it.** When you are unsure where something goes, the answer is in here — do not invent a new location.
4	
5	# 1. Canonical Repository Tree
6	
7	```
8	atlas-erp/
9	├── CLAUDE.md  PLAN.md  PROGRESS.md  DECISIONS.md
10	├── GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md  STRUCTURE.md
11	├── README.md  LICENSE  NOTICE  CONTRIBUTING.md  SECURITY.md
12	├── .gitignore  .env.example  docker-compose.yml  Makefile
13	├── .github/
14	│   ├── workflows/ci.yml
15	│   ├── PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md
16	│   └── ISSUE_TEMPLATE/{bug.yaml,feature.yaml}
17	├── docs/
18	│   ├── architecture.md  api.md  industry-templates.md
19	│   ├── research/s4hana-parity.md
20	│   ├── modules/            # one guide per module: finance.md, inventory.md, ...
21	│   └── assets/             # diagrams/screenshots referenced by docs ONLY
22	├── industry-templates/
23	│   ├── _schema.yaml        # the template JSON-Schema, single source of truth
24	│   └── {manufacturing,retail,professional-services,healthcare,construction}.yaml
25	├── backend/
26	│   ├── pyproject.toml  alembic.ini
27	│   ├── alembic/versions/
28	│   ├── app/
29	│   │   ├── main.py         # app factory + router mounting, nothing else
30	│   │   ├── core/           # cross-cutting only — see §2
31	│   │   └── modules/        # business modules — see §3
32	│   ├── tests/              # mirrors app/ — see §6
33	│   └── seed.py
34	└── frontend/
35	    ├── package.json  vite.config.ts  tsconfig.json  index.html
36	    └── src/
37	        ├── main.tsx  App.tsx  router.tsx
38	        ├── lib/            # api client, auth, query hooks, formatters
39	        ├── components/     # design system, module-agnostic — see §4
40	        └── modules/        # one folder per ERP module, mirrors backend names
41	```
42	
43	Nothing lives outside this tree. No `scratch/`, `tmp/`, `old/`, `backup/`, or `misc/` directories — ever. Temporary experiments happen on a branch and are deleted, not parked in the tree.
44	
45	# 2. `backend/app/core/` — what belongs and what doesn't
46	
47	One file per cross-cutting concern, flat, no subpackages: `config.py`, `db.py` (engine, session, tenant filter), `tenancy.py`, `auth.py`, `rbac.py`, `audit.py`, `events.py` (bus + base event class), `docflow.py`, `models.py` (Base, mixins: TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin), `schemas.py` (shared Pydantic bases, pagination envelope, error envelope), `numbering.py` (document sequences), `money.py` (Money/Quantity/Rate type decorators, quantize + largest-remainder allocate — added by D-015), `custom_fields.py` (custom-field defs registry, validation, JSON column helper — added by D-016), `exceptions.py`, `deps.py` (FastAPI dependencies).
48	
49	**Litmus test:** if a file mentions a specific business concept (invoice, item, employee), it does NOT belong in `core/` — move it to its module. If two modules need the same business logic, the dependency-rule in §5 decides who owns it; `core/` is never the dumping ground.
50	
51	# 3. `backend/app/modules/` — identical anatomy for every module
52	
53	Module package names (fixed, never abbreviate differently elsewhere): `finance`, `inventory`, `procurement`, `sales`, `manufacturing`, `quality`, `maintenance`, `hr`, `projects`, `crm`, `reporting`, `admin`, `industry`.
54	
55	Every module has exactly this internal shape — no exceptions, no creativity:
56	
57	```
58	modules/finance/
59	├── __init__.py
60	├── models.py        # SQLAlchemy models (split into models/ package only if >600 lines: models/journal.py, models/accounts.py, each <400)
61	├── schemas.py       # Pydantic request/response (same split rule)
62	├── service.py       # ALL business logic (split rule: service/ package, one file per aggregate: service/journal.py, service/payments.py)
63	├── router.py        # thin HTTP layer only: parse → call service → return schema
64	├── events.py        # events this module PUBLISHES (definitions) 
65	├── handlers.py      # subscriptions to OTHER modules' events
66	└── constants.py     # enums, status values, magic numbers — no literals inline elsewhere
67	```
68	
69	A new file type may not be invented per-module. If finance needs `depreciation.py`, it goes inside `service/` as `service/depreciation.py`, not as a new top-level module file.
70	
71	# 4. Frontend structure
72	
73	- `src/components/` is the design system: one folder per component (`DataGrid/`, `FormBuilder/`, `Kanban/`, `KpiCard/`, `DocFlowViewer/`), each containing `ComponentName.tsx`, optional `ComponentName.test.tsx`, and `index.ts` re-export. Components here know NOTHING about ERP concepts — they take data and callbacks.
74	- `src/modules/<module>/` mirrors backend module names exactly and contains: `pages/` (route components, named `<Entity>ListPage.tsx`, `<Entity>DetailPage.tsx`, `<Entity>FormPage.tsx`), `components/` (module-specific composites), `api.ts` (typed endpoint calls for this module only), `types.ts` (mirrors backend schemas), `hooks.ts` (TanStack Query hooks: `useJournalEntries`, `usePostJournal`).
75	- `src/lib/`: `apiClient.ts` (the ONLY place fetch/axios appears), `auth.ts`, `queryClient.ts`, `format.ts` (money, dates, quantities — all display formatting goes through here, never inline `toFixed`).
76	- No barrel-exporting whole modules into each other; cross-module UI reuse means the component was design-system material and must be promoted to `src/components/`.
77	
78	# 5. Dependency Rules (what may import what)
79	
80	- `core` imports nothing from `modules`. Modules import `core` freely.
81	- Modules never import each other's `service.py` or `models.py` directly. Cross-module effects go through the event bus (`finance/handlers.py` reacts to `inventory` events). Cross-module reads needed synchronously (e.g., sales needs an item's price) go through a small, explicit query interface the owning module exposes in `modules/<owner>/queries.py` — plus `modules/<owner>/events.py` (declarative event dataclasses only, no logic), the two files another module may import (events.py allowance added by D-011 so handlers can subscribe to typed events).
82	- Dependency direction for queries: finance is the bottom (everyone may use finance/queries), then inventory, then everything else. Two modules may never import each other's queries bidirectionally — if that seems needed, the shared concept is misplaced; file an issue and resolve ownership before coding.
83	- Frontend: `modules/*` may import `lib` and `components`; `components` and `lib` never import from `modules`.
84	
85	# 6. Tests mirror source, exactly
86	
87	`backend/tests/` replicates `app/` paths: code in `app/modules/finance/service/journal.py` is tested in `tests/modules/finance/test_journal.py`. Shared fixtures live in `tests/conftest.py` (db session, tenant factory, auth client) and `tests/modules/<module>/conftest.py` for module fixtures. Test names state the rule being proven: `test_journal_rejects_unbalanced_lines`, `test_posting_to_closed_period_raises`. One assertion-theme per test. Frontend tests sit beside the file they test (`DataGrid.test.tsx`). A regression test for issue #NN includes `#NN` in its docstring/comment.
88	
89	# 7. Naming Conventions (single table of truth)
90	
91	| Thing | Convention | Example |
92	|---|---|---|
93	| Python files/modules | snake_case, singular concern | `journal.py`, `stock_move.py` |
94	| Python classes | PascalCase, no abbreviations | `JournalEntry`, `StockMove`, `PurchaseOrderLine` |
95	| Python functions/vars | snake_case verbs for actions | `post_journal_entry()`, `reserve_stock()` |
96	| Pydantic schemas | Entity + suffix `Create/Update/Read/Filter` | `JournalEntryCreate`, `ItemRead` |
97	| DB tables | snake_case plural, module prefix | `fin_journal_entries`, `inv_stock_moves`, `sls_orders` |
98	| DB columns | snake_case; FKs `<entity>_id`; money pairs `amount`+`currency_code`; booleans `is_/has_` | `is_posted`, `cost_center_id` |
99	| Enums (Py + DB values) | Class PascalCase, values UPPER_SNAKE stored as strings | `OrderStatus.PARTIALLY_SHIPPED` |
100	| Alembic revisions | `NNNN_short_description` sequential | `0007_add_asset_register` |
101	| Domain events | PascalCase past tense, module-prefixed string key | class `SalesOrderShipped`, key `sales.order.shipped` |
102	| Permissions | `module.entity.action` lowercase | `finance.journal.post` |
103	| API routes | `/api/v1/<module>/<resource-kebab-plural>`; actions as sub-resources, never verbs in resource names | `/api/v1/finance/journal-entries/{id}/post` |
104	| JSON fields | snake_case (mirror backend; frontend types match, no camelCase translation layer) | `posting_date` |
105	| TS files | Components PascalCase.tsx, everything else camelCase.ts | `DataGrid.tsx`, `apiClient.ts` |
106	| TS types/interfaces | PascalCase, no `I` prefix | `JournalEntry` |
107	| React hooks | `use` + Entity + verb | `usePostJournalEntry` |
108	| CSS | Tailwind utilities only; the rare custom class kebab-case in one `index.css` | `doc-flow-edge` |
109	| Env vars | `ATLAS_` prefix UPPER_SNAKE | `ATLAS_DATABASE_URL` |
110	| Docs files | kebab-case | `industry-templates.md` |
111	| Branches/commits/labels | as defined in GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md | — |
112	
113	Terminology lock: the same business concept uses the same word everywhere — code, DB, API, UI, docs. It is `item` (not product/article/sku interchangeably), `vendor` (not supplier), `customer`, `warehouse`, `journal entry`. Industry templates may override the *display* label, never the internal name. Record any new canonical term in DECISIONS.md the moment you coin it.
114	
115	# 8. File-Handling Rules
116	
117	1. **Search before create.** Before creating any file, check whether its correct home already exists (`ls`, `grep -r "class JournalEntry"`). Duplicate implementations are a `severity:major` issue.
118	2. **No versioned filenames.** Never `service_v2.py`, `utils_new.py`, `final_fixed.tsx`. Improving a file means editing it; git holds history.
119	3. **No orphan files.** Every file is imported/referenced by something or it doesn't exist. When refactoring away from a file, delete it in the same commit.
120	4. **Size limits.** Hard cap 400 lines per Python file and 300 per TSX component; at the cap, split along the rules in §3/§4 — never split into `part1/part2`.
121	5. **One concept per file.** A file named `journal.py` containing tax logic is misfiled even if it compiles. Filename promises content.
122	6. **Generated files are never hand-edited** (OpenAPI dumps, lockfiles, migration auto-generations get reviewed and adjusted only through their tooling). Commit lockfiles; never commit build output, caches, coverage reports, or `__pycache__` — keep `.gitignore` authoritative.
123	7. **No utils graveyards.** Before adding to a `utils`-like file, ask which module/concern owns the function; `core/` files and `lib/format.ts` are the only sanctioned shared helpers, each scoped by its filename.
124	8. **Imports:** absolute imports only in backend (`from app.modules.finance.service import journal`); frontend uses the `@/` alias (`@/lib/apiClient`). No relative `../../..` chains.
125	9. **Module READMEs are forbidden** — module docs live in `docs/modules/<module>.md` only, so documentation has one home.
126	10. **Renames/moves** are their own commit (`refactor(structure): move costing into inventory/service/costing.py`), never mixed with logic changes, so history stays traceable.
127	11. **Deletions** follow issue-first if the file contains live logic being retired: file the issue, explain replacement, delete in the fix PR.
128	12. **After compaction:** before creating ANY new file, re-read this document and run `git status` + `tree -L 3` (or `find`) to re-anchor on the actual current structure. Never recreate from memory a file that might already exist.
129	
130	# 9. Self-Check (append result to PROGRESS.md at each session end)
131	
132	Any file outside the canonical tree? Any file over the size cap? Any duplicate concept names (`grep` a few suspects)? Any orphan files? Any module breaking the dependency rules? Any term drift (supplier vs vendor)? Each "yes" becomes a `tech-debt` issue per GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md §6, fixed before the next promotion.

83	# --- Query counting (PERFORMANCE §2: the N+1 ban, enforced mechanically) -------

85	
86	@dataclass
87	class QueryCounter:
88	    """Counts real SQL statements executed on the per-test engine while active.
89	
90	    Used as a context manager: ``with query_counter() as qc: ...`` then read ``qc.count``.
91	    The ``after_cursor_execute`` listener attaches to the TEST engine's sync engine on enter
92	    and detaches on exit (per-use, so the per-test engine pattern stays leak-free).
93	    Transaction-control statements (BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK/SAVEPOINT/RELEASE) and PRAGMAs are
94	    excluded — the budget measures real SELECT/INSERT/... statements. ``statements`` keeps
95	    the counted SQL so a budget failure shows exactly which queries ran.
96	    """
97	
98	    sync_engine: Engine
99	    count: int = 0
100	    statements: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
101	
102	    _IGNORED_PREFIXES = ("BEGIN", "COMMIT", "ROLLBACK", "SAVEPOINT", "RELEASE", "PRAGMA")
103	
104	    def _after_cursor_execute(
105	        self,
106	        conn: Any,
107	        cursor: Any,
108	        statement: str,
109	        parameters: Any,
110	        context: Any,
111	        executemany: bool,
112	    ) -> None:
113	        if statement.lstrip().upper().startswith(self._IGNORED_PREFIXES):
114	            return
115	        self.count += 1
116	        self.statements.append(statement)
117	
118	    def __enter__(self) -> "QueryCounter":
119	        self.count = 0
120	        self.statements = []
121	        event.listen(self.sync_engine, "after_cursor_execute", self._after_cursor_execute)
122	        return self
123	
124	    def __exit__(
125	        self,
126	        exc_type: type[BaseException] | None,
127	        exc: BaseException | None,
128	        tb: TracebackType | None,
129	    ) -> None:
130	        event.remove(self.sync_engine, "after_cursor_execute", self._after_cursor_execute)

9	A debit-positive base balance becomes a debit total (and zero credit); a credit-positive one becomes
10	a credit total. No stored totals: re-running after a new posting reflects it immediately.
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	import uuid
16	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
17	from datetime import date
18	from decimal import Decimal
19	
20	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
21	
22	from app.modules.finance.constants import AccountType
23	from app.modules.finance.service.statements.base import (
24	    ZERO,
25	    _account_balances,
26	    load_account_meta,
27	)
28	
29	
30	@dataclass(frozen=True)
31	class TrialBalanceRow:
32	    """One account's line on the trial balance: its code/name/type and the side its net balance
33	    lands on. Exactly one of ``debit``/``credit`` is non-zero (a perfectly netted account is
34	    omitted upstream)."""
35	
36	    account_id: uuid.UUID
37	    account_code: str
38	    account_name: str
39	    account_type: AccountType
40	    debit: Decimal
41	    credit: Decimal
42	
43	
44	@dataclass
45	class TrialBalance:
46	    """The trial balance as of a date (D-021): per-account rows plus the universal-journal
47	    self-check. ``is_balanced`` is the debit==credit identity every posted ledger must satisfy."""
48	
49	    as_of: date
50	    rows: list[TrialBalanceRow] = field(default_factory=list)
51	    total_debit: Decimal = ZERO
52	    total_credit: Decimal = ZERO
53	    is_balanced: bool = True
54	
55	
56	async def trial_balance(
57	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, date_to: date
58	) -> TrialBalance:
59	    """The trial balance for all activity up to and including ``date_to`` (D-021).
60	
61	    Splits each account's signed base balance onto its natural side (a positive debit-positive
62	    balance is a debit total, a negative one a credit total), tagged with the account's code/name/
63	    type. Accounts that net exactly to zero are omitted. Asserts the debit==credit identity into
64	    ``is_balanced`` + the totals — the universal-journal guarantee, not a stored figure."""
65	    balances = await _account_balances(session, tenant_id, date_to=date_to)
66	    meta = await load_account_meta(session, tenant_id)
67	
68	    rows: list[TrialBalanceRow] = []
69	    total_debit = ZERO
70	    total_credit = ZERO
71	    for account_id, signed in balances.items():
72	        account = meta.get(account_id)
73	        if account is None or signed == ZERO:
74	            continue
75	        debit = signed if signed > ZERO else ZERO
76	        credit = -signed if signed < ZERO else ZERO
77	        total_debit += debit
78	        total_credit += credit
79	        rows.append(
80	            TrialBalanceRow(
81	                account_id=account_id,
82	                account_code=account.code,
83	                account_name=account.name,
84	                account_type=account.account_type,
85	                debit=debit,
86	                credit=credit,
87	            )
88	        )
89	
90	    rows.sort(key=lambda r: r.account_code)
91	    return TrialBalance(
92	        as_of=date_to,
93	        rows=rows,
94	        total_debit=total_debit,
95	        total_credit=total_credit,
96	        is_balanced=total_debit == total_credit,
97	    )

1	"""THE single base aggregate every financial statement projects from (D-021).
2	
3	The Universal-Journal payoff (CLAUDE.md rule 1): there are NO stored totals, no balance tables,
4	no materialized views. Every statement — trial balance, P&L, balance sheet, cash flow, cost-centre
5	report, margin — is a projection of ``_account_balances`` over ``fin_journal_lines`` only. One
6	predicate (tenant + ``is_posted`` + date), one projection (functional debit minus credit), one
7	covering index (``ix_fin_journal_lines_proj``); so every statement is provably consistent with the
8	trial balance because they read the SAME query.
9	
10	No header join is needed: the line denormalizes ``tenant_id``/``posting_date``/``is_posted`` during
11	the two-flush posting protocol (D-017), so the aggregate touches the line table alone. MoneyType
12	type propagation keeps the SUM exact on both engines (D-015): NUMERIC on Postgres, scaled-integer
13	micro-units on SQLite, converted back to ``Decimal`` on read.
14	
15	The signed balance is debit-positive: ASSET/EXPENSE accounts (normal DEBIT) carry a positive
16	balance, LIABILITY/EQUITY/REVENUE (normal CREDIT) a negative one. Each statement re-signs per
17	account type as needed (a liability is presented as its credit-positive magnitude, etc.).
18	"""
19	
20	from __future__ import annotations
21	
22	import uuid
23	from dataclasses import dataclass
24	from datetime import date
25	from decimal import Decimal
26	
27	from sqlalchemy import func, select
28	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
29	
30	from app.modules.finance.constants import AccountType, CashFlowCategory, NormalBalance
31	from app.modules.finance.models import Account, AccountGroup, JournalLine
32	
33	# A zero Decimal at the money scale; statement maths reduces onto this so an empty journal yields
34	# explicit zeros rather than None.
35	ZERO = Decimal("0")
36	
37	
38	@dataclass(frozen=True)
39	class AccountMeta:
40	    """The statement-relevant metadata of one account (D-021), loaded once per statement.
41	
42	    Carries everything a projection needs to classify and present a balance: the five-way
43	    ``account_type`` drives which statement the account belongs to; ``normal_balance`` re-signs the
44	    debit-positive base balance into a presentation magnitude; ``cash_flow_category`` and
45	    ``is_cash_equivalent`` feed the indirect cash-flow statement; ``group_id``/``group_code``/
46	    ``group_name`` place the account in the presentation hierarchy."""
47	
48	    account_id: uuid.UUID
49	    code: str
50	    name: str
51	    account_type: AccountType
52	    normal_balance: NormalBalance
53	    cash_flow_category: CashFlowCategory | None
54	    is_cash_equivalent: bool
55	    group_id: uuid.UUID | None
56	    group_code: str | None
57	    group_name: str | None
58	
59	
60	async def _account_balances(
61	    session: AsyncSession,
62	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
63	    *,
64	    date_to: date,
65	    date_from: date | None = None,
66	    posted_only: bool = True,
67	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal]:
68	    """THE base aggregate (D-021): signed (debit-positive) balance per account over the journal.
69	
70	    ``select(account_id, sum(functional_debit - functional_credit)) WHERE tenant, is_posted,
71	    posting_date <= date_to [and >= date_from] GROUP BY account_id``. Every statement builds on
72	    exactly this — same predicate, same projection, same index (``ix_fin_journal_lines_proj``).
73	    Returns ``{account_id: signed_balance}``; accounts with no posting in range are simply absent
74	    (the caller treats a missing key as zero). ``posted_only`` defaults True (statements never show
75	    unposted drafts); it is a parameter only so a future audit view could pass False — it never
76	    does in v1.
77	    """
78	    signed = func.sum(
79	        JournalLine.functional_debit_amount - JournalLine.functional_credit_amount
80	    )
81	    stmt = select(JournalLine.account_id, signed).where(
82	        JournalLine.tenant_id == tenant_id,
83	        JournalLine.posting_date <= date_to,
84	    )
85	    if posted_only:
86	        stmt = stmt.where(JournalLine.is_posted.is_(True))
87	    if date_from is not None:
88	        stmt = stmt.where(JournalLine.posting_date >= date_from)
89	    stmt = stmt.group_by(JournalLine.account_id)
90	
91	    balances: dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal] = {}
92	    for account_id, total in (await session.execute(stmt)).all():
93	        balances[account_id] = Decimal(str(total)) if total is not None else ZERO
94	    return balances
95	
96	
97	async def _dimension_balances(
98	    session: AsyncSession,
99	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
100	    dimension: object,
101	    *,
102	    date_from: date,
103	    date_to: date,
104	    dimension_filter: uuid.UUID | None = None,
105	) -> dict[tuple[uuid.UUID | None, uuid.UUID], Decimal]:
106	    """The base aggregate re-grouped by a line dimension AND account (D-021).
107	
108	    Same predicate and projection as ``_account_balances`` (tenant + ``is_posted`` + date range,
109	    functional debit minus credit), but grouped by ``(dimension_column, account_id)`` so cost-centre
110	    and margin reports read a dimension straight off the journal line. ``dimension`` is the
111	    ``JournalLine`` column object (``JournalLine.cost_center_id`` / ``JournalLine.item_id``);
112	    ``dimension_filter`` narrows to a single dimension value when given. Returns ``{(dim_value,
113	    account_id): signed_balance}``; ``dim_value`` may be None for lines carrying no dimension."""
114	    signed = func.sum(
115	        JournalLine.functional_debit_amount - JournalLine.functional_credit_amount
116	    )
117	    stmt = select(dimension, JournalLine.account_id, signed).where(
118	        JournalLine.tenant_id == tenant_id,
119	        JournalLine.is_posted.is_(True),
120	        JournalLine.posting_date >= date_from,
121	        JournalLine.posting_date <= date_to,
122	    )
123	    if dimension_filter is not None:
124	        stmt = stmt.where(dimension == dimension_filter)
125	    stmt = stmt.group_by(dimension, JournalLine.account_id)
126	
127	    balances: dict[tuple[uuid.UUID | None, uuid.UUID], Decimal] = {}
128	    for dim_value, account_id, total in (await session.execute(stmt)).all():
129	        balances[(dim_value, account_id)] = (
130	            Decimal(str(total)) if total is not None else ZERO
131	        )
132	    return balances
133	
134	
135	async def load_account_meta(
136	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID
137	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, AccountMeta]:
138	    """Every account's statement metadata for a tenant, keyed by id (D-021).
139	
140	    One LEFT JOIN to ``fin_account_groups`` so an account with no group still appears (its group
141	    fields are None). Loaded once per statement and shared across the projection so a statement is
142	    one aggregate query + one metadata query, never per-account lookups."""
143	    stmt = (
144	        select(
145	            Account.id,
146	            Account.code,
147	            Account.name,
148	            Account.account_type,
149	            Account.normal_balance,
150	            Account.cash_flow_category,
151	            Account.is_cash_equivalent,
152	            Account.account_group_id,
153	            AccountGroup.code.label("group_code"),
154	            AccountGroup.name.label("group_name"),
155	        )
156	        .outerjoin(AccountGroup, Account.account_group_id == AccountGroup.id)
157	        .where(Account.tenant_id == tenant_id)
158	    )
159	    meta: dict[uuid.UUID, AccountMeta] = {}
160	    for row in (await session.execute(stmt)).all():
161	        meta[row.id] = AccountMeta(
162	            account_id=row.id,
163	            code=row.code,
164	            name=row.name,
165	            account_type=AccountType(row.account_type),
166	            normal_balance=NormalBalance(row.normal_balance),
167	            cash_flow_category=(
168	                CashFlowCategory(row.cash_flow_category)
169	                if row.cash_flow_category is not None
170	                else None
171	            ),
172	            is_cash_equivalent=bool(row.is_cash_equivalent),
173	            group_id=row.account_group_id,
174	            group_code=row.group_code,
175	            group_name=row.group_name,
176	        )
177	    return meta
178	
179	
180	def presentation_amount(meta: AccountMeta, signed_balance: Decimal) -> Decimal:
181	    """Re-sign the debit-positive base balance into the account's natural presentation magnitude.
182	
183	    ASSET/EXPENSE (normal DEBIT) keep the signed balance; LIABILITY/EQUITY/REVENUE (normal CREDIT)
184	    flip it, so a liability with a -500 base balance presents as +500. Statement bodies show these
185	    natural magnitudes (a positive revenue, a positive liability), while balance/reconciliation
186	    checks run on the raw signed balances where the debit==credit identity holds."""
187	    if meta.normal_balance is NormalBalance.CREDIT:
188	        return -signed_balance
189	    return signed_balance
190	
191	
192	def net_income_signed(
193	    balances: dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal], meta: dict[uuid.UUID, AccountMeta]
194	) -> Decimal:
195	    """Net income (revenue - expense) over whatever range produced ``balances`` (D-021).
196	
197	    Computed straight from the base aggregate: revenue accounts (normal CREDIT) carry a negative
198	    debit-positive balance, expense accounts (normal DEBIT) a positive one, so revenue minus expense
199	    is ``-(Σ revenue signed) - (Σ expense signed)`` = ``-(Σ P&L signed balances)``. Returned as a
200	    credit-positive figure (a profit is positive) — the value the balance sheet folds into retained
201	    earnings and the cash-flow statement starts from."""
202	    pl_signed = ZERO
203	    for account_id, balance in balances.items():
204	        account = meta.get(account_id)
205	        if account is None:
206	            continue
207	        if account.account_type in (AccountType.REVENUE, AccountType.EXPENSE):
208	            pl_signed += balance
209	    return -pl_signed
210

3	Split out of ``service/journal.py`` so the write engine (create/post/reverse) stays under the

5	loaders from here; the router imports the read functions through the ``service`` package surface.

61	    operand. MoneyType result values are Decimal, so the sum is exact (D-015)."""
62	    debit = sum((line.functional_debit_amount for line in lines), Decimal(0))

1	"""AR aging: a pure projection over open customer invoices (PLAN 4.6, D-021 spirit).
2	
3	The AP ``ap_aging.py`` mirror over the receivable side. The aging report derives entirely from the
4	open invoices' ``open_amount`` + ``due_date`` — no stored totals. Each invoice's open balance lands
5	in the bucket for ``as_of - due_date`` days: current (not yet due), 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, over-90; per
6	partner and rolled up. Open amounts are transaction-currency, so a partner with invoices in two
7	currencies appears as two rows (currency rides the grouping key).
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	import uuid
13	from datetime import date
14	from decimal import Decimal
15	
16	from sqlalchemy import select
17	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
18	
19	from app.modules.finance.constants import InvoiceStatus
20	from app.modules.finance.models import CustomerInvoice
21	
22	# Aging bucket upper bounds (days past due) for buckets 1-30 / 31-60 / 61-90; over-90 is the tail.
23	_AGING_BOUNDS: tuple[int, ...] = (30, 60, 90)
24	
25	
26	def _aging_bucket_index(days_overdue: int) -> int:
27	    """Index into (current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, over-90) for ``days_overdue`` (as_of - due_date).
28	    <= 0 is 'current' (index 0); 1..30 -> 1; 31..60 -> 2; 61..90 -> 3; > 90 -> 4."""
29	    if days_overdue <= 0:
30	        return 0
31	    for index, bound in enumerate(_AGING_BOUNDS, start=1):
32	        if days_overdue <= bound:
33	            return index
34	    return 4
35	
36	
37	async def customer_aging(
38	    session: AsyncSession,
39	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
40	    as_of: date,
41	    partner_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
42	) -> dict[str, object]:
43	    """AR aging as of ``as_of`` (PLAN 4.6): bucket each open invoice's open_amount by (as_of -
44	    due_date) into current / 1-30 / 31-60 / 61-90 / over-90, per partner and rolled up. A pure
45	    projection over open invoices — no stored totals. Returns a dict the router maps to
46	    ``ArAgingReportRead``; each partner row keeps its currency (open amounts are transaction-side).
47	    """
48	    stmt = (
49	        select(CustomerInvoice)
50	        .where(
51	            CustomerInvoice.tenant_id == tenant_id,
52	            CustomerInvoice.status.in_(
53	                (InvoiceStatus.POSTED.value, InvoiceStatus.PARTIALLY_PAID.value)
54	            ),
55	            CustomerInvoice.open_amount > 0,
56	        )
57	        .order_by(CustomerInvoice.partner_name)
58	    )
59	    if partner_id is not None:
60	        stmt = stmt.where(CustomerInvoice.partner_id == partner_id)
61	    invoices = list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())
62	
63	    rows: dict[tuple[uuid.UUID, str], tuple[str, list[Decimal]]] = {}
64	    totals = [Decimal(0)] * 5
65	    for invoice in invoices:
66	        days_overdue = (as_of - invoice.due_date).days
67	        bucket = _aging_bucket_index(days_overdue)
68	        key = (invoice.partner_id, invoice.currency_code)
69	        if key not in rows:
70	            rows[key] = (invoice.partner_name, [Decimal(0)] * 5)
71	        amount = Decimal(str(invoice.open_amount))
72	        rows[key][1][bucket] += amount
73	        totals[bucket] += amount
74	
75	    partners = [
76	        {
77	            "partner_id": key[0],
78	            "partner_name": name,
79	            "currency_code": key[1],
80	            "current": buckets[0],
81	            "days_1_30": buckets[1],
82	            "days_31_60": buckets[2],
83	            "days_61_90": buckets[3],
84	            "days_over_90": buckets[4],
85	            "total": sum(buckets, Decimal(0)),
86	        }
87	        for key, (name, buckets) in rows.items()
88	    ]
89	    return {
90	        "as_of": as_of,
91	        "partners": partners,
92	        "current": totals[0],
93	        "days_1_30": totals[1],
94	        "days_31_60": totals[2],
95	        "days_61_90": totals[3],
96	        "days_over_90": totals[4],
97	        "total": sum(totals, Decimal(0)),
98	    }

249	) -> Page[BankStatementLine]:

251	    (the reconciliation work-list; covered by the statement+status composite index)."""
252	    stmt = select(BankStatementLine).where(
253	        BankStatementLine.tenant_id == tenant_id,
254	        BankStatementLine.statement_id == statement_id,
255	    )

258	    return await paginate(

268	
269	async def statement_progress(
270	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, statement_id: uuid.UUID
271	) -> StatementProgress:
272	    """Line counts by status in ONE grouped query (no per-status round trips)."""
273	    rows = (
274	        await session.execute(
275	            select(BankStatementLine.status, func.count(BankStatementLine.id))
276	            .where(
277	                BankStatementLine.tenant_id == tenant_id,
278	                BankStatementLine.statement_id == statement_id,
279	            )
280	            .group_by(BankStatementLine.status)
281	        )
282	    ).all()
283	    by_status = {status: count for status, count in rows}
284	    return StatementProgress(
285	        total=sum(by_status.values()),
286	        unmatched=by_status.get(LineStatus.UNMATCHED.value, 0),
287	        suggested=by_status.get(LineStatus.SUGGESTED.value, 0),
288	        matched=by_status.get(LineStatus.MATCHED.value, 0),
289	        cleared=by_status.get(LineStatus.CLEARED.value, 0),
290	    )
291	
292	
293	async def refresh_statement_status(
294	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, statement: BankStatement
295	) -> StatementProgress:
296	    """Recompute the derived statement status from line resolution (RECONCILED when every line
297	    is MATCHED/CLEARED, PARTIALLY_RECONCILED when some are, else IMPORTED), writing it through
298	    the loaded object + the docflow registry when changed. Re-running it is a no-op."""
299	    progress = await statement_progress(session, tenant_id, statement.id)
300	    if progress.total > 0 and progress.resolved == progress.total:
301	        new_status = StatementStatus.RECONCILED.value
302	    elif progress.resolved > 0:
303	        new_status = StatementStatus.PARTIALLY_RECONCILED.value
304	    else:
305	        new_status = StatementStatus.IMPORTED.value
306	    if statement.status != new_status:
307	        statement.status = new_status
308	        await session.flush()
309	        await docflow.set_document_status(
310	            session, tenant_id, statement.document_id, status=new_status
311	        )
312	    return progress

1	"""The universal journal: header + lines (D-017), the heart of Atlas finance.
2	
3	One append-only line table is the single source of truth for every FI/CO view (D-021); the
4	header carries entry-level lifecycle and the lines carry the postings plus every dimension a
5	statement projects from. Denormalized ``is_posted``/``posting_date``/``fiscal_period_id`` on the
6	line (set during the two-flush posting protocol) let projections query lines with NO header join
7	(D-021), which is why those columns live on the line at all.
8	
9	Money columns use ``MoneyType`` (D-015): exact NUMERIC on Postgres, INTEGER micro-units on
10	SQLite, so the balance trigger's SUM and the one-side CHECK are exact on both engines. For v1,
11	functional amounts EQUAL transaction amounts (single functional currency, posting-time FX
12	translation lands in 4.3) — the columns exist now so the schema and triggers are FX-ready.
13	
14	Constraints declared here (rendered by migration 0009):
15	- ``ck_fin_journal_lines_one_side``: exactly one of debit/credit positive per line, the other
16	  zero — written on the stored columns so it holds on PG NUMERIC and SQLite micro-unit ints.
17	- the per-dialect TRIGGERS (period-open, balance, header immutability, line immutability) are
18	  NOT model constraints; they are hand-written DDL in the migration (D-017/D-018/D-022).
19	
20	Dimension columns (cost_center_id, profit_center_id, project_id, item_id, partner_id) are plain
21	``sa.Uuid`` WITHOUT FKs for now: the CO/project/inventory masters land in later PLAN phases
22	(4.7 controlling, 5 inventory, 11 projects); the ids are stored on the line today and FK'd when
23	those parent tables exist. partner_type + partner_id carry AP/AR open-item linkage (4.4+).
24	"""
25	
26	import uuid
27	from datetime import date, datetime
28	
29	import sqlalchemy as sa
30	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
31	
32	from app.core.docflow import DocumentMixin, document_fk
33	from app.core.models import (
34	    AuditMixin,
35	    Base,
36	    TenantMixin,
37	    TimestampMixin,

45	# Bare CHECK token (the D-022 ck convention wraps it as ck_<table>_<name>). Compares the STORED
46	# representation (NUMERIC on PG, micro-unit INTEGER on SQLite) so "> 0" / "= 0" hold on both.
47	_ONE_SIDE_CHECK = (
48	    "(transaction_debit_amount > 0 AND transaction_credit_amount = 0) "
49	    "OR (transaction_credit_amount > 0 AND transaction_debit_amount = 0)"
50	)

53	class JournalEntry(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, DocumentMixin, Base):
54	    """A journal-entry header (D-017). Registered in core_documents at creation (DocumentMixin)
55	    with doc_number NULL; the gapless ``entry_number`` is claimed at POSTING (D-012), so an
56	    abandoned draft burns no number — hence ``entry_number`` is NULLABLE with a partial unique
57	    index. An entry is single-transaction-currency (cross-currency events become multiple
58	    entries). ``reverses_entry_id`` points at the original an entry reverses;
59	    ``reversed_by_entry_id`` points at the reversing entry — both self composite tenant FKs.
60	    Audited (D-010): every financial mutation is auditable."""
61	
62	    __tablename__ = "fin_journal_entries"
63	    __table_args__ = (
64	        tenant_unique(),
65	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
66	        document_fk(),
67	        # Self composite tenant FKs: a reversal linkage can never cross tenants. Distinct
68	        # explicit names (the D-022 column-0 convention would collide on two self-FKs).
69	        sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
70	            ["tenant_id", "reverses_entry_id"],
71	            ["fin_journal_entries.tenant_id", "fin_journal_entries.id"],
72	            name="fk_fin_journal_entries_reverses_entry_id_fin_journal_entries",
73	        ),
74	        sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
75	            ["tenant_id", "reversed_by_entry_id"],
76	            ["fin_journal_entries.tenant_id", "fin_journal_entries.id"],
77	            name="fk_fin_journal_entries_reversed_by_entry_id_fin_journal_entries",
78	        ),
79	        # Composite tenant FK: the resolved period belongs to the same tenant.
80	        tenant_fk("fin_fiscal_periods", "fiscal_period_id"),
81	        # The gapless-number partial unique index is declared after the class (it needs the
82	        # column object for its dialect partial predicate, expressed without raw SQL so the
83	        # app/modules grep gate stays satisfied — see below).
84	    )

86	    # NULL until posting (D-012 claim-at-permanence); the partial unique index above backstops it.
87	    entry_number: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=True)

97	    description: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(500), nullable=True)
98	    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
99	        sa.String(10), nullable=False, default=EntryStatus.DRAFT.value, server_default="DRAFT"
100	    )
101	    reverses_entry_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
102	    reversed_by_entry_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
103	    posted_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=True)

106	class JournalLine(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
107	    """A journal line (D-017): one posting on one account, one-sided (debit XOR credit). NOT
108	    AuditMixin — lines are written once with their immutable entry and never mutated after the
109	    posting flush, and the header's audit row records the entry-level change; auditing every
110	    line would double the trail with no extra signal (documented exclusion). The denormalized
111	    ``is_posted``/``posting_date``/``fiscal_period_id`` are set during the DRAFT->POSTED flush so
112	    statement projections read lines with no header join (D-021)."""
113	
114	    __tablename__ = "fin_journal_lines"
115	    __table_args__ = (
116	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
117	            "tenant_id",
118	            "journal_entry_id",
119	            "line_number",
120	            name="uq_fin_journal_lines_tenant_id_journal_entry_id_line_number",
121	        ),
122	        tenant_unique(),
123	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
124	        tenant_fk("fin_journal_entries", "journal_entry_id"),

128	    )

130	    journal_entry_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
131	    line_number: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(sa.Integer, nullable=False)
132	    account_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)

136	    # CHECK). MoneyType: exact on both engines so the balance trigger's SUM is exact.
137	    transaction_debit_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(
138	        MoneyType(), nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0"
139	    )
140	    transaction_credit_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(
141	        MoneyType(), nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0"
142	    )

146	        MoneyType(), nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0"
147	    )
148	    functional_credit_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(
149	        MoneyType(), nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0"
150	    )
151	    currency_code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(3), nullable=False)
152	
153	    # Dimensions (all nullable; no FK yet — masters land in later phases, see module docstring).
154	    cost_center_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
155	    profit_center_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
156	    project_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
157	    item_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)

1	"""Accounts Receivable: customer invoices, receipts, allocations and dunning (PLAN 4.6, D-029).
2	
3	The AR sub-ledger mirrors AP (``payables.py``) with the sign flipped: a posted invoice debits the
4	AR control for the gross and credits revenue + output tax (vs AP's Dr expense / Cr AP); a receipt
5	credits AR control and debits the bank (vs AP's Dr AP / Cr bank). Like AP it is keyed by an OPAQUE
6	``partner_id`` (D-029): finance is the bottom of the dependency order, so it never FK-references a
7	customer master (that lives in sales, above finance). Each AR document carries the opaque
8	``partner_id`` plus a denormalized ``partner_name`` for display; the owning module guarantees it.
9	
10	AR adds DUNNING: each open invoice tracks how many dunning notices have been sent
11	(``dunning_level``) and when (``last_dunned_date``). The dunning run (service/dunning.py) advances
12	those as the invoice ages past the day-thresholds; it posts no journal — it only updates state.
13	
14	Every AR document posts through the universal journal (D-017): a ``CustomerInvoice`` registers in
15	core_documents at creation (DocumentMixin) and gets a ``journal_entry_id`` + system number at
16	posting; a ``CustomerReceipt`` is created and posted in one step, clearing the open items its
17	allocations name. Realized FX at clearing (D-019) is computed in the SERVICE, posted inside the
18	receipt journal entry — no extra columns here.
19	
20	Sixth file in the finance ``models/`` package (STRUCTURE §3); re-exported from ``models/__init__``.
21	Money columns use ``MoneyType`` (D-015, exact on both engines). All cross-row links are composite
22	tenant FKs (D-007 backstop) EXCEPT ``partner_id`` (opaque, no FK — D-029) and the dimension ids.
23	Enum-valued columns are plain ``sa.String`` storing the StrEnum value, as elsewhere in finance.
24	"""

28	
29	import sqlalchemy as sa

31	
32	from app.core.docflow import DocumentMixin, document_fk
33	from app.core.models import (

46	class CustomerInvoice(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, DocumentMixin, Base):
47	    """A customer invoice (PLAN 4.6). Registered in core_documents at creation (DocumentMixin,
48	    doc_number NULL); the gapless system ``invoice_number`` is claimed at POSTING (D-012).
49	    ``partner_id`` is the OPAQUE customer id (D-029 — no FK); ``partner_name`` is the denormalized
50	    display name. ``external_ref`` is the tenant's own reference (free text, not unique). At posting
51	    the service builds the AR journal entry (Dr AR control gross, Cr each revenue line net, Cr
52	    output tax), sets ``journal_entry_id`` + ``open_amount`` = gross, flips ``status`` to POSTED.
53	    ``open_amount`` (transaction currency) is the still-owed balance, reduced by receipt allocations
54	    until PAID. ``dunning_level`` is how many dunning notices have been sent (0 = none); the dunning
55	    run raises it as the invoice ages and stamps ``last_dunned_date``. Audited (D-010)."""

79	    partner_name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=False)
80	    # The tenant's own reference on the invoice (free text, not the system number); nullable.
81	    external_ref: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=True)
82	    # The gapless system number, claimed at posting (NULL until then; D-012).

1	"""D-007 tenancy enforcement: context, non-bypassable session filter, write stamping.
2	
3	Three of the four cooperating D-007 layers live here:
4	1. Context — the `current_tenant_id` ContextVar (set by core/deps.py after JWT
5	   validation from PLAN 3.3 on; by `tenant_context()` in tests and seed).
6	2. Read/write filtering — the `do_orm_execute` listener.
7	3. Write stamping — the `before_flush` listener.
8	The fourth layer (composite FKs + the SQLite FK pragma) lives in core/models.py
9	and core/db.py.
10	"""
11	
12	import uuid
13	from collections.abc import Iterator
14	from contextlib import contextmanager
15	from contextvars import ContextVar
16	from itertools import chain
17	
18	from sqlalchemy import event
19	from sqlalchemy.orm import ORMExecuteState, Session, with_loader_criteria
20	
21	from app.core.exceptions import TenancyError
22	from app.core.models import TenantMixin
23	
24	current_tenant_id: ContextVar[uuid.UUID | None] = ContextVar("current_tenant_id", default=None)
25	_system_context: ContextVar[bool] = ContextVar("system_context", default=False)
26	
27	
28	def get_current_tenant_id() -> uuid.UUID | None:
29	    """Active tenant id, fail-closed: raises unless a tenant context is set.
30	    Returns None only while system_context() is active."""
31	    tenant_id = current_tenant_id.get()
32	    if tenant_id is None and not _system_context.get():
33	        raise TenancyError("No tenant context is active")
34	    return tenant_id
35	
36	
37	@contextmanager
38	def tenant_context(tenant_id: uuid.UUID) -> Iterator[None]:
39	    """Run the block as one tenant (tests, seed transaction phase; request handling
40	    sets the ContextVar directly in core/deps.py with middleware reset, per D-007)."""
41	    token = current_tenant_id.set(tenant_id)
42	    try:
43	        yield
44	    finally:
45	        current_tenant_id.reset(token)
46	
47	
48	@contextmanager
49	def system_context() -> Iterator[None]:
50	    """Suspend tenant filtering and write stamping for the block.
51	
52	    Sanctioned in exactly four greppable app call sites (D-007):
53	    1. login user-lookup (core/auth, PLAN 3.3);
54	    2. tenant provisioning in modules/admin (PLAN 14.2);
55	    3. Alembic/seed provisioning phase (seed.py, PLAN 16);
56	    4. event-bus system-event replay (core/events, PLAN 3.6).
57	    Test fixtures may also use it (D-025 tenant_factory). Writers under system
58	    context must set tenant_id explicitly; the composite-FK backstop still applies.
59	    """
60	    token = _system_context.set(True)
61	    try:
62	        yield
63	    finally:
64	        _system_context.reset(token)
65	
66	
67	def _involves_tenant_scoped_entities(execute_state: ORMExecuteState) -> bool:
68	    # all_mappers inspects select() column descriptions / mapper entities AND the
69	    # bind mapper of ORM-enabled update()/delete() — the D-007 involvement rule.
70	    return any(issubclass(m.class_, TenantMixin) for m in execute_state.all_mappers)
71	
72	
73	def _filter_tenant_statements(execute_state: ORMExecuteState) -> None:
74	    """do_orm_execute listener: inject the tenant predicate into every ORM
75	    select/update/delete; fail-closed when tenant-scoped entities are touched
76	    without a tenant context."""
77	    if not execute_state.is_orm_statement:
78	        # Core statements bypass by design: sanctioned only inside core/ with
79	        # explicit tenant_id, bounded by the D-007 grep gate.
80	        return
81	    if execute_state.is_column_load or execute_state.is_relationship_load:
82	        # Refresh and lazy loads inherit the criteria propagated from their
83	        # originating statement; re-injecting here would break attribute refresh.
84	        return
85	    if not (execute_state.is_select or execute_state.is_update or execute_state.is_delete):
86	        return
87	    if _system_context.get():
88	        return
89	    tenant_id = current_tenant_id.get()
90	    if tenant_id is None:
91	        if _involves_tenant_scoped_entities(execute_state):
92	            raise TenancyError("Tenant-scoped statement executed without a tenant context")
93	        # Statements touching only non-tenant tables (Alembic bookkeeping, the
94	        # tenants root) legitimately run with no tenant context.
95	        return
96	    execute_state.statement = execute_state.statement.options(
97	        with_loader_criteria(
98	            TenantMixin,
99	            # The ContextVar is read above, in this per-execution listener — the
100	            # lambda-SQL system forbids invoking .get() inside the lambda itself.
101	            # track_closure_variables=False keeps the closure value out of the
102	            # statement cache key, so each execution binds the fresh tenant id
103	            # instead of baking in the first value seen (pinned by a test).
104	            lambda cls: cls.tenant_id == tenant_id,
105	            include_aliases=True,
106	            track_closure_variables=False,
107	        )
108	    )
109	
110	
111	def _stamp_tenant_on_flush(session: Session, flush_context: object, instances: object) -> None:
112	    """before_flush listener: stamp tenant_id on new tenant-scoped instances and
113	    reject any new/dirty instance whose tenant_id differs from the context."""
114	    if _system_context.get():
115	        # Provisioning/seed/system writes set tenant_id explicitly; the composite
116	        # FK backstop still rejects ids that do not exist in adm_tenants.
117	        return
118	    active = current_tenant_id.get()
119	    for obj in chain(session.new, session.dirty):
120	        if not isinstance(obj, TenantMixin):
121	            continue
122	        if active is None:
123	            raise TenancyError("Tenant-scoped instance flushed without a tenant context")
124	        if obj.tenant_id is None:
125	            obj.tenant_id = active
126	        elif obj.tenant_id != active:
127	            raise TenancyError(
128	                "Instance tenant_id differs from the active tenant context",
129	                code="tenancy.tenant_mismatch",
130	            )
131	
132	
133	def install_tenancy_guards() -> None:
134	    """Attach both listeners to the sync Session class — AsyncSession proxies it,
135	    so every execute call and relationship load is covered. Idempotent so repeated
136	    calls cannot double-register. Invoked at import time of app.core.db: every
137	    engine/session factory in app, tests and seed is built from that module, so no
138	    session can exist unguarded (models.py cannot host the call — this module
139	    imports TenantMixin from it, which would be an import cycle)."""
140	    if not event.contains(Session, "do_orm_execute", _filter_tenant_statements):
141	        event.listen(Session, "do_orm_execute", _filter_tenant_statements)
142	    if not event.contains(Session, "before_flush", _stamp_tenant_on_flush):
143	        event.listen(Session, "before_flush", _stamp_tenant_on_flush)

1	"""Async engine and session plumbing.
2	
3	Every engine the app touches (runtime, tests, migrations) is built via build_engine
4	or has enable_sqlite_foreign_keys attached, so the SQLite FK pragma backstop of
5	D-007 can never be silently absent.
6	"""
7	
8	from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
9	from typing import Any
10	
11	from sqlalchemy import Engine, event
12	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import (
13	    AsyncEngine,
14	    AsyncSession,
15	    async_sessionmaker,
16	    create_async_engine,
17	)
18	
19	from app.core.audit import install_audit_guards
20	from app.core.config import get_settings
21	from app.core.tenancy import install_tenancy_guards
22	
23	# Import side effect ON PURPOSE: every engine/session factory in app, tests and
24	# seed is built via this module, so importing it guarantees the D-007 + D-010 listeners
25	# exist before any session can be constructed. tenancy.py itself cannot self-install
26	# from models.py (import cycle), and main.py would leave direct-session users
27	# (tests, seed, alembic) unguarded.
28	#
29	# Order is load-bearing (D-010): tenancy first so its before_flush STAMPS tenant_id, then
30	# audit so its before_flush fires AFTER and reads a settled tenant_id. before_flush
31	# listeners fire in registration order, so this call order is the guarantee.
32	install_tenancy_guards()
33	install_audit_guards()
34	
35	
36	def _set_sqlite_fk_pragma(dbapi_connection: Any, connection_record: Any) -> None:
37	    cursor = dbapi_connection.cursor()
38	    cursor.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
39	    cursor.close()
40	
41	
42	def enable_sqlite_foreign_keys(engine: Engine) -> None:
43	    """SQLite enforces FK constraints only with this per-connection pragma (D-007)."""
44	    if engine.dialect.name == "sqlite":
45	        event.listen(engine, "connect", _set_sqlite_fk_pragma)
46	
47	
48	def build_engine(url: str, **kwargs: Any) -> AsyncEngine:
49	    """The single sanctioned way to create an engine; attaches the FK pragma listener."""
50	    engine = create_async_engine(url, **kwargs)
51	    enable_sqlite_foreign_keys(engine.sync_engine)
52	    return engine
53	
54	
55	def build_session_factory(engine: AsyncEngine) -> async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession]:
56	    return async_sessionmaker(engine, expire_on_commit=False)
57	
58	
59	engine = build_engine(get_settings().database_url)
60	session_factory = build_session_factory(engine)
61	
62	
63	async def get_session() -> AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]:
64	    """FastAPI dependency. Commits belong to the unit-of-work helper (later task);
65	    here: yield, roll back on exception, always close via the context manager."""
66	    async with session_factory() as session:
67	        try:
68	            yield session
69	        except Exception:
70	            await session.rollback()
71	            raise
72	
73	
74	def get_session_factory() -> async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession]:
75	    """FastAPI dependency returning the runtime sessionmaker. D-013's idempotency reserve()
76	    needs a SEPARATE short-lived session that COMMITs immediately (so concurrent duplicates
77	    collide on the reservation PK independently of the request's business transaction). It
78	    opens that session from this factory. Exposed as a dependency — not imported directly —
79	    so the test harness overrides it to the per-test engine's factory the same way it
80	    overrides get_session, keeping the reservation in the same database as the business work."""
81	    return session_factory
82	
83	
84	# Register the D-013 idempotency model and the 4P.5 jobs model on Base.metadata HERE rather than
85	# via core/models' trailing import: core/idempotency imports THIS module for its session
86	# dependencies and core/jobs imports core/audit (the actor ContextVar), while this module imports
87	# core/audit -> core/models — so the registration must happen AFTER db/audit/tenancy finish
88	# loading (the bottom of this file) to avoid the import cycle. Side-effect imports only — the
89	# names bind the model classes so alembic env.py and the engine bootstrap see the tables.
90	from app.core import idempotency as _idempotency  # noqa: E402,F401
91	from app.core import jobs as _jobs  # noqa: E402,F401

1	"""D-012 document registry, flow links, and chain traversal.
2	
3	The registry turns the polymorphic (doc_type, doc_id) problem into ordinary FK integrity:
4	every business document row links to exactly one ``core_documents`` registry entry via the
5	NOT NULL ``document_id`` FK supplied by ``DocumentMixin``. Predecessor/successor edges live
6	in ``core_doc_links``, so chain traversal is one generic recursive CTE over two narrow
7	tables — the ACDOCA-era Document Relationship Browser shape — with zero module-aware code in
8	core (core imports nothing from modules).
9	
10	Claim-timing (D-012): a document is registered with ``doc_number`` NULL at creation;
11	documents with a draft lifecycle are numbered at posting via the numbering claim, documents
12	permanent at creation are numbered immediately. The partial unique index on
13	``(tenant_id, doc_number)`` is the DB backstop turning any numbering bug into a constraint
14	violation.
15	
16	The ORM models live HERE rather than in core/models.py: models.py is near its ~350-line
17	soft cap, so the D-012 entities sit in their concern file (consistent with numbering.py and
18	sanctioned by the PLAN). Noted in DECISIONS.md.
19	"""
20	
21	import uuid
22	from dataclasses import dataclass
23	
24	import sqlalchemy as sa
25	from sqlalchemy import select
26	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
27	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, declared_attr, mapped_column

30	    Base,
31	    TenantMixin,
32	    TimestampMixin,
33	    UuidPKMixin,
34	    tenant_fk,
35	)

37	# Depth ceiling on chain traversal (D-012): real chains are <10 nodes; the cap plus the
38	# visited-path cycle guard make a malformed graph terminate instead of spinning.
39	_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH = 20

41	
42	class Document(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):

44	    constant (``'sales.order'``, ``'finance.journal_entry'``) declared in module
45	    constants.py; ``doc_id`` is the PK of the business row in its own table; ``doc_number``
46	    is assigned at posting (NULL until then); ``status`` is the registry-level status string.
47	
48	    Not AuditMixin: the registry mirrors business rows that are themselves audited — the
49	    document's own table carries the audited business state, so auditing the registry too
50	    would double-record (documented exclusion)."""

53	    __table_args__ = (

55	        # column 0 only and would collide with tenant_unique()).

57	            "tenant_id", "doc_type", "doc_id", name="uq_core_documents_tenant_id_doc_type_doc_id"

187	async def register_document(
188	    session: AsyncSession,
189	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
190	    doc_type: str,
191	    doc_id: uuid.UUID,
192	    *,
193	    doc_number: str | None = None,
194	    status: str | None = None,
195	) -> Document:
196	    """Insert a registry row for a business document and return it (D-012). Called by the
197	    creating service in the same transaction as the business-row insert (the DocumentMixin
198	    NOT NULL FK makes skipping it a hard error). ``doc_number`` is left NULL for draft-
199	    lifecycle documents (numbered later at posting) and set for documents permanent at
200	    creation. A Core insert sets tenant_id explicitly — core/docflow is a D-007 sanctioned
201	    raw-SQL site."""
202	    document_id = uuid.uuid4()
203	    await session.execute(
204	        sa.insert(Document.__table__).values(
205	            id=document_id,
206	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
207	            doc_type=doc_type,
208	            doc_id=doc_id,
209	            doc_number=doc_number,
210	            status=status,
211	        )
212	    )

214	        await session.execute(select(Document).where(Document.id == document_id))
215	    ).scalar_one()

229	    posting) — passing ``doc_number`` here writes it through the partial-unique (tenant,
230	    doc_number) backstop, so any numbering bug surfaces as a constraint violation. Only the
231	    provided arguments are changed (``None`` leaves the column untouched, except doc_number which
232	    is always set when supplied). A Core UPDATE addressed by (tenant_id, id) — a D-007 sanctioned
233	    explicit-tenant raw-SQL site."""
